gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures 15, 16, 18 and 19 carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

The chassis width. The datasheet's Table 2 says 17.26 in (43.8 cm); the guide's Table 7 says 19.03 in (48.33 cm), which is 17.26 in plus the front brackets (the rack-requirements table states 19 in over the brackets). The datasheet's 17.26 in is used because the photograph's scale is consistent with it; the depth differs by 0.01 in (25.52 against 25.51), and the datasheet's is used.
The maximum power of the QFX5240-64QD. Guide Table 13 says 2258 W; the datasheet says 2242 W. Same measure and same scope (maximum, 40 C, IMIX traffic). The guide's 2258 W is used.

The AC input of the supply. Guide Table 4 says 200 to 240 VAC at 16 A maximum; guide Table 13 says an operating range of 200 to 277 VAC and 6 A at 200 VAC, 3.8 A at 240 VAC; the datasheet says 180 to 264 VAC. Table 4's range is carried on the supply and every reading is kept in the device's `power-input-ac`.
The type of the two small cages. The guide's callout 2 calls them "SFP28 ports" and its text and the datasheet call them "2 x 10-Gbps SFP+ ports". They are modelled as SFP+ at 10 Gbps.

Which ports take high power optics. The guide's note says that only the front-panel ports in the middle rows support them and lists 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10 and so on to 61 and 62, which are ports of the second and third rows in a column of four, counting from 0. The note is carried in `features.optics-qsfp-dd` and the face does not mark those ports, because the metal does not.

The DC supply. The datasheet's ordering table lists QFX5241-PWR-DC-AO as "QFX5240 Series-2RU DC PSU, Air Out"; the QFX5240 hardware guide describes AC supplies only and no photograph of a DC build is held.

The lamps of the management jack. Guide figure 14 and Table 10 describe lamps on the management port; the photograph shows them at the corners of the upper jack. The jack is drawn with the library's lamped jack.

The connector type of the 1PPS and 10MHz jacks. The guide calls them "clock input and output connectors"; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated.
The rating label of each supply and the serial number labels (figures 45 to 48). Not drawn.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5240-2U-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.

chassis.note: datasheet Table 2: 17.26 x 3.46 x 25.52 in (43.8 x 8.8 x 64.8 cm), 2RU, 22 kg (48.50 lb) fully loaded without optics. The inch figures are used. The guide's Table 7 prints the same height and weight and a width of 19.03 in (48.33 cm) and a depth of 25.51 in (65 cm); 19.03 in is the width over the front brackets, which is the rack-face width the datasheet's 17.26 in leaves out, so the datasheet's body width is used and brackets are not modelled. The depth differs by 0.01 in; the datasheet's 25.52 in is used.

colour.note: The front plate samples #6b7480 (a bare patch near the foot) and the rear panel #646d79. The chassis colour is the front's. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figures 4 and 5 are the same studio photographs at reduced size and agree with them. The guide calls the SFP pair "SFP28 ports" in its callouts and the text and the datasheet say SFP+ 10 GbE; the group is stated at 10g. The photograph shows the supplies' hubs carrying the supply maker's name; it is a third party's logo and is not drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kit QFX5240-2U-4PRMK (a four-post tool-less kit, Table 6 and the datasheet's ordering table). The library holds no contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

earthing.note: Two threaded studs 15.5 mm apart on a pad at the left of the rear, under the ground symbol, 6.4 mm from the left edge. The guide's grounding section (figure 1 and Ground the QFX5240 Switch) calls for two M6 screws with star washers and a Panduit LCDXN2-14AF-E lug, which is a two-hole lug on 5/8 in centres; the 15.5 mm pitch of the photograph agrees. The guide's text puts the terminal "on the side of the chassis" and "through the left-front mounting bracket"; the photograph and the guide's figure 1 show it on the rear panel, and the photograph is followed.

front-green-tab.note: The green tab at the foot of the management panel, 17.0 mm wide and 2.7 mm tall, is the chassis serial number pull-out (callout 8 of figure 7). It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between the left and right edges, is 1893 px wide and 375 px from the top edge to the bottom lip, an aspect of 5.05 against the datasheet's 438.4 / 87.9 = 4.99 (1 percent out). Scale 4.318 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge (x 115 px) and the top edge (y 192 px). The rear photograph's body is 1895 px wide, 4.323 px/mm. The guide's figures 2 to 5 are half-tone thumbnails and are used only to count and read. Had 19.03 in been the body width the scale would be 3.92 px/mm and the cages 26.5 mm apart.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. The guide, published 2026-07-10, and the datasheet, March 2026, state none and no Juniper notice was found in the intake. The device states none announced. Estimated, because absence in the documents is not a notice from the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper right of the face, above the model name QFX5240-64QD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the last column, from the top: the model name under the maker's logo, the RJ-45 management port with a USB-A port under it in one shield (MGMT, and the USB 3 symbol), the stacked SFP+ pair with 64 and 65 below it, a strip with the legends ID, SYS and ALM above three lamps and the RST pinhole, the 1PPS and 10MHz coaxial jacks, the RJ-45 console (CON) and time-of-day (TOD) jacks stacked in one shield, and a green serial-number tab at the foot (guide figure 7 callouts 1 to 9). The USB tongue is blue in the photograph, which is the USB-IF colour of a 3.0 port; the guide says "USB port" only.

modules.note: The four fan modules (QFX5240-2U-FANAO) and the two power supplies (QFX5240-PWR-AC-AO) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component (guide Table 6). Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside.

port-lamps.note: Each network port has a single RGB lamp (guide, QFX5240 Network Port LEDs, Table 8): in the photograph a dot 2.0 mm across at the left of each cage, at the height of the cage's centre, 1.85 mm left of the cell. The lamps are unlit. The SFP+ ports show no lamp and the guide describes none.

port-numbering.note: Printed on a strip above the upper band and a strip below the lower band, read off the photograph: over each column "N up-arrow ... down-arrow N+1" with N a multiple of four, and under each column the same with N+2. So a column holds ports 4c to 4c+3 from the top, the upper band's pair first; the SFP+ pair prints "64 up-arrow" and "down-arrow 65" under it. The guide's Tables 6 and 7 name them network ports and SFP28 ports (callouts 1 and 2), and its text names the SFP+ ports 10 GbE. Interface names are not printed and none is stated in the guide, so they are not recorded.

ports.note: Front photograph: 64 QSFP-DD openings, sixteen columns of four on a 103.7 px pitch, 24.01 mm, each opening 80 px (18.5 mm) wide; the cage cell is the registry's 19.0 mm, set so the opening centres agree, and the first cell starts at 11.35 mm. A column holds two stacked pairs, one above the other, with a gap between them (figures 4 and 7). The two SFP+ cages stand to the right of the last column, stacked, one above the other (callout 2, 14.5 mm wide).

power.note: Guide Table 13: typical 616 W and maximum 2258 W at 220 to 240 V for the QFX5240-64QD. The datasheet's power table says typical 616 W and maximum 2242 W (maximum measured at 40 C with DR optics, typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load, excluding transceivers). The maxima differ (2258 and 2242 W); the guide's is used. AC input: guide Table 4 says 200 to 240 VAC at 16 A maximum, guide Table 13 says 200 to 277 VAC with 6 A at 200 VAC and 3.8 A at 240 VAC, and the datasheet says 180 to 264 VAC.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.323 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 5: two supplies stacked at the left end, supply 0 above supply 1, an earthing pad with two studs and the ground symbol under them, then four fan modules numbered 0 to 3 from the left on an 85.7 mm pitch. A fan symbol, the module number and an arrow are printed beside each fan opening, and a power symbol with the supply number beside each supply. The fan plates measure 80.3 mm wide and 80.0 mm high; the supplies 73.7 mm wide and 39.5 mm high.

row-pitch.note: Down column 5 the four openings centre at 18.5, 35.9, 52.1 and 69.5 mm: 17.4 mm between the two cages of a pair, 16.2 mm from a pair to the next, so the rows are laid on 17.4 mm inside each band, the upper band 13.5 mm and the lower 47.1 mm from the top. The registry gives no belly-to-belly pitch for a QSFP-DD cage.

sources.note: QFX5240 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-07-10, 147 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2026), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5240/qfx5240.pdf: the front and rear figures 2 to 5, the port panel figures 6 to 13 and Tables 8 and 9 (lamps), Table 3 (hardware models), Tables 4 to 6 and 13 (power and cooling) and Table 7 (physical specifications). The QFX5240 line of Switches datasheet, a00150802ENW Rev. 2, 12 pages (Juniper Networks, published 2026-03; HPE document), from https://www.hpe.com/psnow/doc/a00150802enw: Table 2 (system capacity and dimensions), the power table and the ordering information. Juniper's studio photographs of the 64QD, front and rear (qfx5240-64qd-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 735 px, and qfx5240-64qd-rear-high.jpg, from juniper.net's image library). The documents and the photographs are the maker's and public; the guide and datasheet carry a copyright notice and no terms of use beyond it, so only facts are transcribed. No Visio stencil, 3D model or mechanical drawing is held for the QFX5240. The guide's figures are half-tone thumbnails of the same photographs.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the grey latch mesh between the two cages of every pair, so both lips face the band between them: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention. The convention is applied, not observed. The SFP+ pair is the same.

variants.note: Guide Table 3 and datasheet ordering information: QFX5240-64QD-AO (AC, airflow out) and the spare QFX5240-64QD-CHAS, "Spare chassis without PSU and fans". Both share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. NOT MODELLED: the QFX5241-64QD (-AO, -DO, -DO-T2, -CHAS, -TCHAS), a sibling the guide's note and the datasheet name with its own part numbers and a DC supply, which has its own hardware guide and is left to its own slice; and the DC supply the datasheet lists for the series (QFX5241-PWR-DC-AO), which the QFX5240 guide does not describe.

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the top above the cages, a band along the bottom, a column at the left edge, a column at the right edge and a field under the clock connectors. Drawn as vent decor in those positions, pitched to the photograph and estimated.
